title: Connected fibres from formal functions and idempotents
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be proper, and assume $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=R$. Then every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), lines 15334--15357; the formal-functions input is Cohomology Lemma 30.4.1 (Tag 02OD), and the proper-fibre idempotent input is Derived Categories Lemma 21.16.1 (Tag 0G7X)

proof.text: Factor the proper morphism through the relative spectrum of its global sections using [lem-weil-pbc-stein-universally-closed-factor]. In the hypothesis $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=R$, this relative spectrum is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ itself, and the factorization lemma makes the resulting morphism surjective. Therefore every scheme-theoretic fibre is nonempty.

To prove connectedness, suppose a fibre has a nontrivial clopen decomposition and take its characteristic idempotent. The proper-fibre idempotent image lemma [lem-weil-pbc-stein-fibre-idempotent-image] lifts this idempotent to the stalk of $f_*\mathcal O_X$. Properness gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness [pqf-lem-proper-basic], so pushforward preserves quasi-coherent modules [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh]. The universal factorization [lem-weil-pbc-stein-universally-closed-factor], specialized to $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=R$, identifies the pushforward algebra with $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$; the affine relative-spectrum and tilde/global-sections identifications [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec] [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] therefore identify its stalk with the local ring $R_s$.

source.place: Theorem 37.53.5 (Tag 03H2), normalized affine reduction, lines 15321--15342, using Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY)

proof.text: Let $r\in R_s$ be the lifted idempotent. Since $R_s$ is local, either $r$ is a unit or $r\in\mathfrak m_s$. By the fibre definition [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the residue-field quotient [def-weil-residue-field], the map $R_s\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ factors through $\kappa(s)=R_s/\mathfrak m_s$. If $r$ is a unit, its image is a unit and an idempotent unit is $1$; if $r\in\mathfrak m_s$, its image is $0$. Thus the image is $0$ or $1$, contradicting the characteristic idempotent from [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent], which is $1$ on one nonempty clopen piece and $0$ on the other. Hence the fibre is connected.
